summary:
Mato Grosso recorded 3 killings of trans and travesti people in 2025 on a population of ~3.6 million - about 0.83 per million per year, more than double the national rate, and the 2024 dossier counted 8 killings in the state, its highest year. The state sits on the Cerrado/agribusiness frontier, where the dossier's finding that most killings happen outside the capitals means small-town exposure is relevant for visitors travelling beyond Cuiabá.

Three cases on a small population is statistically fragile, and no qualitative incident, ordinance or enforcement evidence was found beyond the ANTRA counts; the elevated per-capita reading therefore carries a smaller weight than the raw rate suggests.

sources.summary: ANTRA's 9th annual dossier (released 26 Jan 2026, reported by SBT News): Brazil recorded 80 murders of trans and travesti people in 2025, 34% down on 2024 but with at least 75 attempted homicides and crimes marked by excessive violence; per-state 2025 counts - Ceara and Minas Gerais 8 each, Bahia and Pernambuco 7 each, Goias, Maranhao and Para 5 each, Alagoas 2, Mato Grosso 3; 1,261 murders over 2017-2025 (avg 140/year); 97% of victims travestis/trans women, over half aged 18-29, 70% Black among racially-identified cases; 67.5% of killings happened in interior cities rather than capitals, where monitoring, denunciation and access to public policies are harder; Brazil has led the global ranking since 2008. Lists Mato Grosso at 3 killings for 2025.

ANTRA 2024 dossier coverage (27 Jan 2025): 122 trans and travesti people murdered in Brazil in 2024, 16% below 2023's 145 and just under the 2008-2024 average of 125; five victims were human-rights defenders, including a city-council alternate; 95.9% of victims were travestis/trans women; worst states: Sao Paulo 16, Minas Gerais 12, Ceara 11, with no records in Acre, Rio Grande do Norte or Roraima; at least 68% (83 cases) occurred in interior cities outside state capitals; 1,179 killings confirmed 2017-2024; official statistics are unreliable due to misclassification and underreporting. Supplies the 2024 national baseline and interior pattern; the year's per-state table places Mato Grosso among the worst performers.
